labs.decisionNote: Prefer a measured germination comparison; a tropism option would change the main question.

options.title: Seeds under different water conditions
options.activity: Compare germination and root growth under controlled water conditions.
options.learningEvidence: A fair test, germination counts and an explanation supported by real observations.
options.virtualChange: Retain the question; replace fixed virtual timing and doses with an actual growing protocol.

options.title: Upright Petri-dish growth investigation
options.activity: Track roots and shoots through upright dishes and graph measurements over several days.
options.learningEvidence: Separate germination percentage from subsequent growth.
options.virtualChange: Add root/shoot measurements and a classroom observation schedule.

options.title: Rotate seedlings to investigate gravitropism
options.activity: Use the upright-dish method to investigate root growth after the dish is rotated.
options.learningEvidence: Explain a directional growth response rather than whether a seed germinates.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around plant responses and growth direction if this becomes the main pairing.

labs.decisionNote: Two measurement options and one related surface demonstration; avoid treating drops as a calibrated force measurement.

options.title: Water and detergent on coins
options.activity: Count retained drops and compare matched coins with and without detergent.
options.learningEvidence: Connect measured differences with attraction among water molecules.
options.virtualChange: Use actual dropper measurements; the virtual drop size is not a physical calibration.

options.title: Floating paper clip and detergent
options.activity: Observe a supported paper clip and predict how detergent changes the surface.
options.learningEvidence: Explain why surface behavior changes; distinguish it from density alone.
options.virtualChange: Add a qualitative support-and-collapse comparison instead of the current drop-count table.

options.title: Water versus alcohol on coins
options.activity: Compare how two liquids spread and how many drops remain on a matched surface.
options.learningEvidence: Relate molecular properties to observed surface behavior.
options.virtualChange: Add a liquid-polarity comparison and its own school-approved handling plan.

labs.decisionNote: Food-test controls are the closest match; microscopy or vitamin C would change the evidence collected.

options.title: Unknown food with positive and negative controls
options.activity: Use approved indicator tests to compare known controls with selected unknown foods.
options.learningEvidence: Use several tests to justify limited claims about biological molecules.
options.virtualChange: Adapt the college-level resource to school equipment and the exact assays used in our lab.

options.title: Starch in ripe and unripe banana cells
options.activity: Compare stained banana smears and record visible starch grains.
options.learningEvidence: Explain how a stain provides evidence and how samples can differ.
options.virtualChange: Narrow the question to starch and add microscopy observations; this does not test all macromolecules.

options.title: Compare vitamin C in foods
options.activity: Use a reviewed vitamin-C investigation to compare food samples.
options.learningEvidence: Design a chemical comparison and explain what the test actually detects.
options.virtualChange: Redesign the assay, controls and question around a vitamin rather than the current macromolecule panel.

labs.decisionNote: Preserve calibrated measurement; a microscope activity should require observations that answer a question.

options.title: Plant and prepared animal cell comparison
options.activity: Measure visible cells in prepared/wet-mounted specimens using the existing classroom route.
options.learningEvidence: Calibrated sizes, observed structures and honest sample limits.
options.virtualChange: Use the existing classroom entry; teacher confirms specimen preparation and calibration.

options.title: Measure cells in different onion layers
options.activity: Compare epidermal cell dimensions from different onion layers.
options.learningEvidence: Use calibrated measurements to test an explanation for tissue growth.
options.virtualChange: Replace the specimen comparison with a growth question; simplify the post-16 resource for grade 9.

options.title: Pondweed focal planes and chloroplast movement
options.activity: Focus through a leaf and observe how cell structures and movement appear.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish optical sections from the whole three-dimensional specimen.
options.virtualChange: Add focal-plane or movement evidence instead of treating a drawing as a single complete cell.

labs.decisionNote: Preserve the reviewed lab and accepted A/D wording. These are optional alternative pairings, not corrections to it.

options.title: Dialysis tubing and selective transport
options.activity: Use a reviewed membrane investigation and record mass change and/or indicator movement.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish water movement from solute passage and justify membrane limits.
options.virtualChange: Keep the accepted concentration comparison; document the actual tubing and classroom observations.

options.title: Shell-less egg osmosis
options.activity: Compare prepared eggs in contrasting solutions and record their change.
options.learningEvidence: Explain water movement across a membrane using observations.
options.virtualChange: Replace dialysis apparatus, preparation time and data tables; do not reuse its model numbers.

options.title: Agar cubes and diffusion distance
options.activity: Compare penetration into different-sized agar blocks.
options.learningEvidence: Explain diffusion distance and surface-area-to-volume effects.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around diffusion and cell size; this is not the same evidence as osmotic mass change.

labs.decisionNote: Keep the existing catalase-temperature comparison as the closest route; other variables require a new question.

options.title: Potato catalase at different temperatures
options.activity: Use the documented gas collector to compare early reaction rates.
options.learningEvidence: Use actual initial rates and apparatus limits to support an enzyme explanation.
options.virtualChange: Keep the existing entry and perform the documented local teacher pilot.

options.title: Catalase with different substrate concentrations
options.activity: Collect oxygen from matched potato preparations with different peroxide conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Interpret substrate concentration and reaction rate while controlling enzyme amount.
options.virtualChange: Change the treatment variable and graphs from temperature to concentration.

options.title: pH and starch breakdown by amylase
options.activity: Measure an iodine-test endpoint for starch breakdown under different pH conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Relate enzyme conditions to an explicitly defined endpoint.
options.virtualChange: Change enzyme, substrate, units and question; a new virtual design would be needed for a close pairing.

labs.decisionNote: Both are suitable gas-production comparisons; gas method and sugar concentration must remain clear.

options.title: Matched sugar types with gas collection
options.activity: Compare yeast with the existing control/glucose/sucrose plan and actual gas measurements.
options.learningEvidence: Use a control and time series to reason about fermentation.
options.virtualChange: Use the current classroom collector sheet for the apparatus chosen.

options.title: Fermentation across sucrose concentrations
options.activity: Measure fermentation under differing sucrose conditions using the publisher investigation.
options.learningEvidence: Separate a sugar-amount effect from a sugar-identity effect.
options.virtualChange: Add concentration as the treatment and revise the question and analysis.

labs.decisionNote: Choose between gas-related flotation evidence and starch accumulation; they are different proxies.

options.title: Floating leaf disks under different light conditions
options.activity: Record flotation over time using the existing light/control comparison.
options.learningEvidence: Explain the meaning and limits of flotation and ET50.
options.virtualChange: Use actual preparation and unreached endpoints rather than imposing model values.

options.title: Leaf disks with changed carbon-dioxide availability
options.activity: Use the leaf-disk technique to compare a carbon-source treatment.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish the investigated factor from other limits on photosynthesis.
options.virtualChange: Add carbon availability and its controls; retain the distinction between flotation and direct photosynthetic rate.

options.title: Light, darkness and starch in leaves
options.activity: Use small leaf samples to compare starch evidence in light/dark conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Interpret starch accumulation rather than short-term gas buildup.
options.virtualChange: Redesign the measurement, timescale and questions around starch; this is not an ET50 replacement.

labs.decisionNote: Gibberellin is the current model. Phototropism or touch responses are good alternatives with different questions.

options.title: Documented dwarf-plant signal/carrier comparison
options.activity: Track stem growth in matched plants given an educational signal preparation or its carrier.
options.learningEvidence: Explain an effect using change from starting height and independent plants.
options.virtualChange: Retain current guidance; source the correct plant stock and follow supplier directions.

options.title: Seedling response to directional light
options.activity: Investigate bending under defined light conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Use a controlled observation to explain a plant response.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around directional growth and light response; it is not a direct test of added gibberellin.

options.title: Seedling response to mechanical stimulation
options.activity: Use the published project starter to compare growth after controlled touch conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Explain changes in plant growth from evidence rather than intention.
options.virtualChange: Develop a new stimulus/treatment plan and virtual response model.

labs.decisionNote: Counting real fields and investigating a treatment answer different questions; keep fields as samples rather than independent plants.

options.title: Prepared root-tip stage counts
options.activity: Classify and count mitotic stages in non-overlapping prepared-slide fields.
options.learningEvidence: Use stage proportions and explain the assumptions behind duration estimates.
options.virtualChange: Use the existing classroom counts and keep fields separate.

options.title: Environmental factor and onion-root cell division
options.activity: Adapt the onion-root investigation in the Cancer Storyline to compare a defined factor.
options.learningEvidence: Connect experimental design with cell division evidence.
options.virtualChange: Add treatment-level replication and a causal question; simplify the broader storyline to grade 9.

options.title: Physical chromosome and cell-division model
options.activity: Use paper chromosome components to show duplication and separation.
options.learningEvidence: Explain what the microscope stages represent mechanistically.
options.virtualChange: Use as a supplement, or redesign the virtual task around mechanisms rather than estimating proportions.

labs.decisionNote: Prefer an explicit chromosome model for crossing over; offspring-building activities need an added recombination step.

options.title: Existing chromosome-strip crossing-over model
options.activity: Exchange corresponding nonsister chromosome segments and follow the modeled cell divisions.
options.learningEvidence: Track inherited allele combinations and distinguish the modeled egg/sperm pathways.
options.virtualChange: Use the current paper model; retain chromosomes, nuclei and centromeres in the correct relationships.

options.title: Build-a-Chromosome movement model
options.activity: Use paper DNA/chromosomes and the guide’s recombination extension.
options.learningEvidence: Explain homolog pairing and exchange rather than swapping random pieces.
options.virtualChange: Select and scaffold the relevant extension and add the current pathway distinctions.

options.title: Reebop offspring and variation
options.activity: Build fictional offspring from inherited allele combinations.
options.learningEvidence: Explain why related offspring can differ.
options.virtualChange: Add crossing over or broaden the virtual question: basic Reebops is not a full model of recombination.

labs.decisionNote: Keep the reviewed corn investigation as the closest pairing; the alternatives use different evidence or trait models.

options.title: Documented corn-ear phenotype counts
options.activity: Count phenotypes on corn from a known cross and compare independent ears.
options.learningEvidence: Support an inheritance-ratio claim while retaining sample variation.
options.virtualChange: Keep the reviewed collection/analysis; verify the actual cross before choosing its expected ratio.

options.title: Segregation in corn pollen
options.activity: Use the published pollen-starch investigation to observe allele segregation.
options.learningEvidence: Link meiotic segregation with observed classes.
options.virtualChange: Replace kernel counting with pollen microscopy, its phenotype evidence and appropriate expected counts.

options.title: Model families with Reebops
options.activity: Combine modeled parental alleles and construct offspring traits.
options.learningEvidence: Connect genotype, phenotype and variation across a class.
options.virtualChange: Use modeled family data rather than claiming to measure the current corn cross.

labs.decisionNote: Use a supplied-image/data route when live crossing is not practical. Gene distance is not established by a physical chromosome craft alone.

options.title: Educational two-point Drosophila cross
options.activity: Score parental/recombinant offspring from a documented educational cross.
options.learningEvidence: Estimate recombination from classified offspring and explain sample limits.
options.virtualChange: Allow cross lead time; adapt sex-linked details and the current trait definitions.

options.title: Printed offspring-photo mapping investigation
options.activity: Classify a prepared, cross-labeled photograph set and calculate recombination.
options.learningEvidence: Use scored evidence and retain ambiguous cases.
options.virtualChange: Author a verifiable image/data pack; this is our proposed adaptation, not a supplied ready-made photo lesson.

labs.decisionNote: The stable ID refers to fruit extraction. Preserve the no-detergent and blank comparisons and the limits of crude material.

options.title: Controlled fruit extraction with comparison samples
options.activity: Use the existing complete preparation and its no-detergent/blank controls.
options.learningEvidence: Explain mechanical disruption, membranes, separation and precipitation.
options.virtualChange: Retain controls; visible crude material is not a purity or DNA-concentration measurement.

options.title: Publisher plant-material extraction method
options.activity: Use the published bulk-extraction method as an alternative classroom preparation.
options.learningEvidence: Relate each separation step to the material observed.
options.virtualChange: Choose one reviewed recipe and keep comparable controls; do not combine incompatible recipes or add unnecessary repeated extractions.

labs.decisionNote: Cell-free expression is the direct practical route; paper models are useful when kit equipment is unavailable.

options.title: BioBits Central Dogma expression investigation
options.activity: Use the kit’s supported fluorescence observations to investigate gene expression.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish transcription and protein-expression evidence.
options.virtualChange: Use only actual kit-supported comparisons and timing; retain controls and label ordinal versus instrument readings.

options.title: Paper transcription and translation
options.activity: Build an RNA message and translate a short sequence with paper components.
options.learningEvidence: Explain how sequence information is used to produce a peptide.
options.virtualChange: Replace brightness evidence with sequence/process evidence and an appropriate report.

options.title: Protein structure/function engineering
options.activity: Investigate predicted fluorescent-protein changes with the published kit.
options.learningEvidence: Connect protein sequence/structure with an observed function.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around structure/function rather than the present expression-control question.

labs.decisionNote: The current lab models an arabinose-controlled reporter. Its legacy ID must not turn this into a claimed lac-operon experiment.

options.title: pGLO reporter induction and selection
options.activity: Compare reporter-bearing/control cells under the kit’s supported plate conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish gene presence, selection, growth and induced expression.
options.virtualChange: Use the approved kit protocol and actual arabinose system; maintain the current distinctions.

options.title: Plate-evidence card investigation
options.activity: Sort provided plate images by growth and fluorescence and justify the controls.
options.learningEvidence: Use evidence to separate transformation/selection from expression.
options.virtualChange: Create a labeled evidence pack from reviewed images or original artwork; no culture handling is needed for this proposed route.

labs.decisionNote: Actual DNA, simulated dye samples and paper-band analysis are useful options with different limits.

options.title: Prepared DNA with a ladder
options.activity: Run prepared DNA samples and estimate sizes from a calibrated ladder.
options.learningEvidence: Use migration measurements and interpolation rather than visual matching alone.
options.virtualChange: Use existing guidance with actual supplier equipment/stain settings.

options.title: Dye electrophoresis mystery
options.activity: Separate the kit’s dye mixtures and compare band patterns in a fictional case.
options.learningEvidence: Practice loading, polarity and separation while interpreting model evidence.
options.virtualChange: Identify dyes as simulated samples; do not convert dye mobility into actual DNA base-pair size.

options.title: Paper ladder calibration and unknown bands
options.activity: Measure original, scale-labeled band images and estimate an unknown within the ladder range.
options.learningEvidence: Demonstrate calibration and explain uncertainty.
options.virtualChange: Author or obtain an appropriate image/data set; this proposed worksheet does not practice physical gel loading.

labs.decisionNote: Retain the reviewed virtual-only core unless you choose otherwise. These can be classroom supplements; none automatically replaces every enzyme/location task.

options.title: Paper transcription and translation
options.activity: Manipulate paper DNA, RNA and translation components.
options.learningEvidence: Use complementary sequences and codons to explain information transfer.
options.virtualChange: Supplement the current lab; add replication, processing and location tasks if chosen as a complete alternative.

options.title: Central dogma card sorting
options.activity: Arrange process and molecule cards and explain their relationships.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish DNA replication, transcription and translation.
options.virtualChange: Use as an explanation check; include enzyme placement and sequence evidence separately.

options.title: Cell-free gene-expression experiment
options.activity: Observe the kit’s actual transcription/translation reporter evidence.
options.learningEvidence: Connect molecular information with a measured or scored output.
options.virtualChange: Cell-free reactions do not model a nucleus or RNA export; redesign location-specific claims if this becomes the primary pairing.

labs.decisionNote: Prepared material and images can both support the sampling question; culturing is not required for the basic route.

options.title: Prepared Sordaria cross-slide counts
options.activity: Classify ordered asci in non-overlapping fields from a prepared educational cross.
options.learningEvidence: Connect segregation patterns, sampling and the centromere-distance estimate.
options.virtualChange: Use existing scoring guidance and keep uncertain/excluded asci visible.

options.title: Printed ascus-image scoring and comparison
options.activity: Count and classify a documented set of real or clearly labeled teaching images.
options.learningEvidence: Compare independent fields without selecting only clear or unusual patterns.
options.virtualChange: Author an image sampling pack and answer key; distinguish schematic data from actual cross images.

labs.decisionNote: The beak-tool model is the closest published match. A feeding contest needs an explicit link to inheritance and later generations.

options.title: Beaks as tools and changing food supply
options.activity: Collect model food with contrasting tools and compare success across environments.
options.learningEvidence: Explain environment-dependent advantage using measured class results.
options.virtualChange: Add a clear inheritance/offspring step to pair fully with our next-generation task.

options.title: Rock pocket mouse populations over time
options.activity: Count and analyze coat-color patterns in supplied population scenes.
options.learningEvidence: Explain selection from differences in survival and inherited variation.
options.virtualChange: Redesign the virtual context and evidence around camouflage and time-series populations.

options.title: Lizard limb traits and habitats
options.activity: Graph a selected subset of published lizard measurements on paper.
options.learningEvidence: Support a habitat/trait comparison from real data.
options.virtualChange: Change the virtual question from feeding and generations to comparative trait evidence.

labs.decisionNote: The publisher offers a physical demonstration alongside a digital tool; only the marble demonstration is proposed as the classroom activity.

options.title: Two-color marble drift demonstration
options.activity: Use the educator demonstration to follow allele sampling through model generations.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish chance changes from an advantage-based selection rule.
options.virtualChange: Align the sampling rules, counts and population comparisons with our model.

options.title: Repeated small versus large gene pools
options.activity: Use our proposed repeated bead draws from matched starting allele pools.
options.learningEvidence: Compare variation among independent population histories.
options.virtualChange: Author a classroom protocol and collector sheet; NHGRI supplies scientific background, not this ready-made activity.

options.title: Founder or bottleneck event investigation
options.activity: Use a clearly labeled extension that sharply samples a model population, then follows later draws.
options.learningEvidence: Explain lost variation without assuming that removed alleles were less useful.
options.virtualChange: Add a named founder/bottleneck event and compare it with ordinary drift.

labs.decisionNote: Strong card activities exist. Some DNA-tree resources use software, so a paper version needs prepared evidence rather than a digital-only link.

options.title: Shell cards and proposed evolutionary groups
options.activity: Use printable shell cards to propose and revise a relationship tree.
options.learningEvidence: Justify grouping from characters and identify uncertain inferences.
options.virtualChange: Retain tree comparisons and avoid treating overall resemblance as sufficient evidence.

options.title: Finch evidence cards and evolutionary relationships
options.activity: Use the published finch inquiry and cards to reason about species relationships.
options.learningEvidence: Connect ecological and trait evidence with an explanatory model.
options.virtualChange: Select the tree-reasoning portions and scaffold the wider inquiry for grade 9.

options.title: Prepared DNA alignment on paper
options.activity: Compare a short teacher-prepared alignment and test alternative trees.
options.learningEvidence: Use sequence characters as a second evidence source.
options.virtualChange: Author a paper subset; the publisher’s full molecular activity includes online analysis.

labs.decisionNote: A network-spread activity and a cell-level release model address different scales; retain that distinction.

options.title: Graphing disease spread on a network
options.activity: Track a modeled spread event, graph relationships and test a prevention change.
options.learningEvidence: Explain how contact structure affects transmission.
options.virtualChange: Align network rules and the prevention comparison; use fictional rather than personal contact data.

options.title: Viral lysis and budding with components/cards
options.activity: Use the published demonstration to compare release from host cells.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish host-cell processes and different release mechanisms.
options.virtualChange: Adjust the pathogen context and molecular components; do not imply that every virus uses the same cycle.

labs.decisionNote: I found useful morphology and DNA-identification resources, but no verified ready-made nonculture packet that duplicates our fictional metabolic profiles. The closest match needs an original evidence pack.

options.title: Fictional microbe evidence-card mystery
options.activity: Compare original cell images, structure descriptions and supplied test-result cards.
options.learningEvidence: Use several evidence types to distinguish profiles without claiming a clinical identification.
options.virtualChange: Develop and review the packet; OpenStax is background, not a published protocol for this exact activity.

options.title: Build bacterial shapes and arrangements with manipulatives
options.activity: Use the published candy/manipulative model to describe bacterial morphology.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish shapes and arrangements using consistent observations.
options.virtualChange: Broaden or narrow the virtual question to morphology; shape alone does not identify our metabolic profiles.

options.title: DNA-identification case on paper
options.activity: Use teacher-prepared sequence/test evidence inspired by the identification workflow.
options.learningEvidence: Explain why sequence evidence can distinguish organisms.
options.virtualChange: This is an original paper adaptation of a digital lab; redesign around molecular evidence instead of our current profile tests.

labs.decisionNote: Several genuine microscopy options exist. Fixed slides can show structure; they cannot show live movement.

options.title: Protist survey with live observations
options.activity: Compare approved educational protist specimens and record visible structures and locomotion.
options.learningEvidence: Connect movement with observed structures and state identification limits.
options.virtualChange: Align specimens, scale calibration and observation categories with the current comparison.

options.title: Observe living material in a hanging drop
options.activity: Use the published preparation to observe movement with less compression.
options.learningEvidence: Explain how preparation affects what can be observed.
options.virtualChange: Scaffold the post-16 technique and use approved specimens; add a fair motion-observation plan.

options.title: Preying protozoa: feeding behavior
options.activity: Compare feeding behaviors in the publisher’s educational specimens.
options.learningEvidence: Use direct observations to compare cellular strategies.
options.virtualChange: Redesign or extend the virtual question around feeding rather than locomotion alone.

labs.decisionNote: The spore print and yeast observations offer different life-history evidence; neither should become an edibility test.

options.title: Mushroom spore-print investigation
options.activity: Make and compare prints using the published activity and a defined observation question.
options.learningEvidence: Connect visible patterns with microscopic spores and reproductive structures.
options.virtualChange: Add time, specimen maturity and uncertain-result notes; a print is not species or edibility proof.

options.title: Budding yeast under the microscope
options.activity: Use the publisher’s yeast-cell investigation to observe budding and other cell features.
options.learningEvidence: Compare asexual budding with spore-based examples.
options.virtualChange: Add yeast microscopy and an explicit comparison with the current fungal examples.

options.title: Hyphae, mycelium and fruiting-body stations
options.activity: Compare prepared images/slides and original labeled mushroom observations.
options.learningEvidence: Explain relationships among fungal structures.
options.virtualChange: Author the station sheets and reviewed image set; the botanical-garden resource is scientific background.

labs.decisionNote: Specimen stations and model cards are good matches; observing a complete life cycle needs far more time than one class.

options.title: Fern fronds, sori and spores
options.activity: Inspect suitable specimens/prepared material using the university laboratory reference.
options.learningEvidence: Identify the sporophyte and connect sori with spores.
options.virtualChange: Build a grade-9 worksheet; UBC supplies reference observations rather than our complete class protocol.

options.title: Fern gametophytes and young sporophytes
options.activity: Compare prepared gametophytes and young sporophytes or suitable documented images.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish life-cycle generations and structures.
options.virtualChange: Source the missing stages or images and simplify the university terminology.

options.title: Moss/fern life-cycle floor or card model
options.activity: Arrange original stage cards and label meiosis, gametes, fertilization and ploidy.
options.learningEvidence: Explain where the life-cycle transitions occur.
options.virtualChange: Author the card set and check organism-specific details; do not equate spores with gametes.

labs.decisionNote: Both physical design options are plausible; use actual fall/drift observations rather than the virtual model’s numerical targets.

options.title: Design wind-dispersed model seeds
options.activity: Build and test simple dispersal designs from the published activity.
options.learningEvidence: Use controlled comparisons to connect structure with movement.
options.virtualChange: Define mass, release conditions, measurement and meaningful repeats.

options.title: Paper-helicopter design investigation
options.activity: Compare a defined rotor-design variable using paper helicopters.
options.learningEvidence: Measure descent and explain the limits of a seed analogy.
options.virtualChange: Connect the rotor explicitly with winged seeds; a Mars/helicopter context alone does not teach plant dispersal.

labs.decisionNote: Published general sorting lessons are useful but do not fully replace evidence about symmetry, tissues and internal body cavities. This pairing needs careful scope selection.

options.title: Anatomical evidence stations
options.activity: Compare original specimen images and sections showing the target body-plan traits.
options.learningEvidence: Justify classifications from visible anatomical evidence.
options.virtualChange: Author a scientifically reviewed station set; the chapter provides background, not a complete activity.

options.title: NPS classification systems inquiry
options.activity: Sort organisms and explain the observations used to construct groups.
options.learningEvidence: Show why classifications require explicit characters.
options.virtualChange: Deepen the middle-school task for grade 9 or redesign the virtual around general classification instead of internal body plans.

options.title: Shell sorting and evolutionary grouping
options.activity: Use the printed shell activity to compare character-based groupings.
options.learningEvidence: Explain how a classification proposal can be supported or revised.
options.virtualChange: Change the main virtual question toward evolutionary relationships; shell appearance does not show every internal body-plan trait.

labs.decisionNote: A classroom key-building task and a field key-use task are both strong options; use observable characters.

options.title: Build and peer-test a dichotomous key
options.activity: Use the NPS picture-based process to build and test a key.
options.learningEvidence: Demonstrate that paired choices identify a new example reliably.
options.virtualChange: Use invertebrate examples and enough detail for grade 9.

options.title: Use and evaluate a real field key
options.activity: Use the NPS tree-key field activity as a method model, or choose a reviewed local invertebrate key.
options.learningEvidence: Explain uncertain identifications and limits of observable features.
options.virtualChange: A tree version changes the organism group; align the virtual examples if it becomes the main pairing.

labs.decisionNote: Comparative anatomy and ecological trait graphs are useful, but they support different kinds of claim.

options.title: Scaled homologous-limb comparison
options.activity: Measure corresponding bones in original scale-labeled images or replicas.
options.learningEvidence: Use homologous parts while distinguishing size, proportion and function.
options.virtualChange: Create a reviewed image/replica pack; a reference photograph is not a complete measurement protocol.

options.title: One Bone, Two Bones observation and explanation
options.activity: Use the published image phenomenon for a student-generated structural explanation.
options.learningEvidence: Identify a common skeletal pattern in a modified limb.
options.virtualChange: Author an evidence question; do not measure absolute lengths without a valid scale.

options.title: Lizard limb measurements across habitats
options.activity: Graph a prepared subset of published species measurements.
options.learningEvidence: Support a trait/habitat comparison using real data.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around ecological trait variation rather than the current cross-vertebrate homology question.

labs.decisionNote: Water uptake, mass loss and stomatal density are distinct measurements. Choose the evidence first.

options.title: Moving-bubble potometer
options.activity: Compare water uptake under a defined environmental change.
options.learningEvidence: Use a controlled rate measurement and explain the uptake/transpiration connection.
options.virtualChange: Use teacher-prepared apparatus and actual units; uptake is an indirect indicator.

options.title: Gravimetric water-loss comparison
options.activity: Use a reviewed mass-loss setup to compare plant water loss.
options.learningEvidence: Explain water balance and apparatus/evaporation controls.
options.virtualChange: Add mass/time observations and preserve the distinction from a bubble displacement reading.

options.title: Count stomata in leaf impressions
options.activity: Estimate stomatal density in calibrated microscopic fields.
options.learningEvidence: Use counts per area and explain variation among leaf surfaces or specimens.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around leaf structure; stomatal counts alone do not measure transpiration rate.

labs.decisionNote: Strong soil activities exist, but infiltration, retained water and engineered amendments answer different questions.

options.title: Biochar and measured soil-water behavior
options.activity: Use the published design activity to compare a soil amendment with an appropriate control.
options.learningEvidence: Use water measurements to evaluate a soil-function claim.
options.virtualChange: Add amendment conditions and distinguish retention from drainage.

options.title: Field infiltration comparison
options.activity: Adapt the USDA field method to compare water entering selected soil locations.
options.learningEvidence: Explain infiltration rate using observed time and field conditions.
options.virtualChange: Change the question and apparatus from retained water in columns to infiltration in place; adapt equipment for school use.

options.title: Design a water-retaining hydrogel
options.activity: Use the published engineering sequence to investigate a water-retaining material.
options.learningEvidence: Evaluate a designed solution with measured evidence.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around materials and water conservation; the full source is a multi-session sequence.

labs.decisionNote: All three are useful; dissection and pollen transfer do not by themselves demonstrate fertilization.

options.title: Flower structure observation/dissection
options.activity: Locate and compare flower structures using a reviewed specimen method.
options.learningEvidence: Connect observed structures with reproductive roles.
options.virtualChange: Extend the primary-level resource with grade-9 explanations and distinguish unseen processes.

options.title: Observe and measure pollen-tube growth
options.activity: Observe suitable pollen and compare tube growth with the published method.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish pollen germination/tube growth from pollen transfer.
options.virtualChange: Add actual microscopy evidence, suitable seasonal specimens and its own timing.

options.title: Pollination role-play game
options.activity: Use a physical role-play to trace pollen transfer among flowers.
options.learningEvidence: Explain transfer paths and compare a model with real structures.
options.virtualChange: Deepen the primary-level game and add fertilization evidence separately if covering the entire current question.

labs.decisionNote: A close cooling practical needs an original controlled protocol. Diffusion and dinosaur data are good chapter options but should not be described as the same heat-loss experiment.

options.title: Controlled cooling in matched container shapes
options.activity: Measure cooling for defined container sizes and calculate geometric ratios.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish total area, area per volume and temperature change.
options.virtualChange: Author and pilot the protocol; OpenStax supplies background, not this ready-made classroom experiment.

options.title: Agar-cell diffusion and surface-area-to-volume ratio
options.activity: Compare how far a visible diffusion front penetrates model cells.
options.learningEvidence: Use size and geometry to explain a transport limit.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around diffusion rather than heat transfer if this is the main practical.

options.title: Use scientific evidence to investigate dinosaur thermoregulation
options.activity: Analyze the educator activity’s supplied evidence about temperature regulation.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish physical cooling from biological thermoregulation claims.
options.virtualChange: Review the educator-submitted resource and redesign toward data-based inference, not the present two-cube calculation.

labs.decisionNote: A starch endpoint is a strong match; a model gut adds absorption and membrane transport.

options.title: Amylase activity under different pH conditions
options.activity: Track a defined starch-test endpoint with reviewed enzyme conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Use controls and a time-based rate interpretation.
options.virtualChange: Align the virtual treatments with the chosen enzyme investigation and actual endpoint method.

options.title: Food digestion in a model gut
options.activity: Use the published food/amylase investigation with a membrane compartment.
options.learningEvidence: Separate digestion evidence from transport across a model barrier.
options.virtualChange: Add absorption/transport questions and label the membrane and chemical-test models.

options.title: Banana ripening and visible starch grains
options.activity: Compare stained plant samples at different ripeness stages.
options.learningEvidence: Use an observation to support a limited claim about starch.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around plant carbohydrate change; this is not an isolated test of amylase action.

labs.decisionNote: A ruler response and a Stroop task measure different combinations of perception and action.

options.title: Ruler-drop reaction-time investigation
options.activity: Record catch distances and use an appropriate distance/time conversion.
options.learningEvidence: Compare repeated measurements and explain anticipation and apparatus limits.
options.virtualChange: Replace browser-event timing with physical catch data and its assumptions.

options.title: Printed Stroop interference comparison
options.activity: Compare timed naming of suitable printed color/word conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Explain interference and distinguish response choice from a simple detection task.
options.virtualChange: Create a printable version from the source approach and redesign the virtual around attention/choice effects.

labs.decisionNote: The existing virtual perception task can pair with a paper demonstration; a wider visual-field activity changes the question.

options.title: Printed dot/cross blind-spot demonstration
options.activity: Record disappearance/reappearance with fixed viewing conditions and measured distance.
options.learningEvidence: Connect the observation with the optic-disc model.
options.virtualChange: Supply scale and viewing instructions and retain the activity’s approximate, nonclinical interpretation.

options.title: What fills in the missing visual region?
options.activity: Use the source’s line/pattern variations through the blind-spot region.
options.learningEvidence: Explain the difference between missing retinal input and perceived continuity.
options.virtualChange: Add a perception explanation task rather than only a boundary calculation.

options.title: Peripheral vision limits
options.activity: Use the published angle-based activity to compare detection of different visual information.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish peripheral detection from the anatomical blind spot.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around visual fields and stimulus properties; these are different phenomena.

labs.decisionNote: Three strong classroom models are available; none requires testing students’ blood.

options.title: Keep It Balanced card game
options.activity: Use the Smithsonian endocrine/homeostasis game and explain the strategy used.
options.learningEvidence: Reason about regulation rather than memorizing a hormone name.
options.virtualChange: Match the game’s simplifications with the virtual insulin/glucagon and storage model.

options.title: Blood-glucose board model and scenarios
options.activity: Use the university board/pasta model for meal, fasting and selected challenge scenarios.
options.learningEvidence: Explain interacting organs and feedback from model changes.
options.virtualChange: Select grade-9 scenarios and separate physiological modeling from personal health interpretation.

options.title: Whole-class glucose-regulation role play
options.activity: Act out roles and trace the movement of signals and glucose.
options.learningEvidence: Explain a coordinated feedback response across parts of a system.
options.virtualChange: Review and simplify the archived educator resource; add individual evidence rather than credit for taking a role.

labs.decisionNote: A measured lever is the closest match. A hydraulic limb is a useful engineering alternative but changes the mechanism.

options.title: Model elbow with measured force and attachment points
options.activity: Use an original hinged-arm apparatus to compare effort at different lever arms.
options.learningEvidence: Use measurements to explain turning effects and force tradeoffs.
options.virtualChange: Author the apparatus/procedure and retain explicit model limits; the lesson supplies mechanical background.

options.title: Simple-lever mechanical-advantage investigation
options.activity: Use the publisher lesson and associated practical to compare effort/load distances.
options.learningEvidence: Support a mechanical-advantage claim using evidence.
options.virtualChange: Add a clear connection to muscle attachment and an arm rather than treating every lever as anatomically identical.

options.title: Build hydraulic artificial limbs
options.activity: Construct and evaluate the published syringe-actuated limb design.
options.learningEvidence: Explain how an engineered actuator moves a joint.
options.virtualChange: Redesign toward prosthetic/hydraulic engineering; a syringe is not a contracting muscle.

labs.decisionNote: The two published models show different ways to inflate a balloon. Their pressure mechanisms must be distinguished.

options.title: Diaphragm bottle-and-balloon model
options.activity: Change the model cavity volume and observe the balloon response.
options.learningEvidence: Explain pressure, volume and airflow with a causal model.
options.virtualChange: Author the student observation/report task and discuss the rigid-bottle limitations.

options.title: Syringe-driven interactive lung box
options.activity: Use the publisher’s second model to move air directly into/out of balloons.
options.learningEvidence: Compare active air delivery with a changing-cavity model.
options.virtualChange: Distinguish positive-pressure air delivery from ordinary diaphragm-driven inspiration.

labs.decisionNote: A controlled water-tube practical is a close original proposal; the published obstruction activity has a different engineering objective.

options.title: Tube diameter and driving-pressure investigation
options.activity: Measure outflow from defined tubes under controlled head/pressure conditions.
options.learningEvidence: Separate diameter and pressure effects and distinguish rate from speed.
options.virtualChange: Author and pilot the setup; the physics source is not a ready-made school protocol or a human blood model.

options.title: Let the Blood Flow: blocked-tube engineering
options.activity: Use the published model to investigate removing an artificial obstruction.
options.learningEvidence: Evaluate a proposed solution from flow observations.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around blockage and engineering rather than the current ideal diameter/pressure comparison.

labs.decisionNote: No verified full wet-lab counterpart was found for filtration plus selective reabsorption and secretion. Prefer a whole-nephron model, or deliberately narrow/redesign the virtual around membrane transport.

options.title: Nephron substance-accounting board
options.activity: Move original labeled tokens through filtration, reabsorption and secretion steps.
options.learningEvidence: Account for each substance and explain the different transport processes.
options.virtualChange: Develop the board, rules and checks; the chapter is background, not a published ready-to-use activity.

options.title: Selective membrane transport with dialysis tubing
options.activity: Use a reviewed membrane experiment to compare passage of different solutes/water.
options.learningEvidence: Explain selective passage using observed evidence.
options.virtualChange: Narrow the virtual question if chosen as the main pairing: this does not demonstrate nephron pressure filtration, reabsorption or secretion.

labs.decisionNote: The immune-cell card resource is a strong match. An antibody-detection assay would shift the question away from memory.

options.title: Smallpox, immune-cell cards and vaccination evidence
options.activity: Build an immune-response sequence and relate it to the activity’s graphs/stories.
options.learningEvidence: Explain memory-cell roles using both process and response evidence.
options.virtualChange: Scaffold the AP-level terms and keep the initial/later-response comparison explicit.

options.title: First versus later response on a tabletop timeline
options.activity: Use an original printed-cell and response-curve timeline based on the reference module.
options.learningEvidence: Explain why a later response can differ from a first response.
options.virtualChange: Author the paper activity; the linked module is digital and is not itself a ready-made physical lesson.

options.title: Educational ELISA antibody detection
options.activity: Use the educational kit’s samples and controls to interpret a detection result.
options.learningEvidence: Explain binding specificity and the function of assay controls.
options.virtualChange: Redesign toward antibody detection; one positive assay does not demonstrate immune memory or protection.

labs.decisionNote: The current virtual uses a sea-urchin example. Human clay activities are useful related options, not interchangeable stage diagrams.

options.title: Sea-urchin cleavage and gastrulation model
options.activity: Use original clay/paper sections to show smaller cells and distinct cell movements.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish cleavage, ingression and invagination and track tissue origins.
options.virtualChange: Build and review a sea-urchin-specific activity using our current evidence; the image resource is supporting observation, not a complete protocol.

options.title: Synchronized Division image investigation
options.activity: Use the published early-embryo image to develop questions and explain division evidence.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish observed cell patterns from assumed timing or later movements.
options.virtualChange: Add suitable supplied sections for gastrulation if covering the full current question.

options.title: Human gastrulation with modeling clay
options.activity: Adapt the published collegiate model of cellular/tissue movements.
options.learningEvidence: Use a three-dimensional representation to explain development.
options.virtualChange: Simplify heavily for grade 9 and redesign the organism/stage context; human and sea-urchin development cannot be mixed.

labs.decisionNote: Field observations, gradients and an animal choice experiment answer related but different questions.

options.title: Compare local microhabitats with quadrats
options.activity: Use a reviewed random-sampling method and measure selected abiotic conditions in two areas.
options.learningEvidence: Support a limited habitat/abundance comparison with actual samples.
options.virtualChange: Adapt species and instrument methods to the site; field correlations alone do not prove a cause.

options.title: Investigate a local environmental gradient
options.activity: Use a schoolyard transect to compare abundance and an abiotic condition along a gradient.
options.learningEvidence: Explain spatial patterns and the sampling method.
options.virtualChange: Adapt the published transect technique to a local site; the source’s saltmarsh context and post-16 detail are not adopted wholesale.

options.title: Humidity choice in pill bugs
options.activity: Use the published choice-chamber experiment with approved educational specimens.
options.learningEvidence: Distinguish an observed behavioral response from field distribution.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around a controlled animal-behavior question if selected; it is not a direct test of the current habitat survey.

labs.decisionNote: The bean model is an unusually close published match; a quadrat alternative changes the method and organism assumptions.

options.activity: Use the published simulation and compare an estimate with a known model total.
options.learningEvidence: Explain mixing, recapture, sampling variation and assumptions.
options.virtualChange: Align sample sizes and recording; avoid unnecessary repeated setup while retaining meaningful independent samples.

options.title: What happens when capture is biased?
options.activity: Use an original extension in which some model individuals have a different capture chance.
options.learningEvidence: Explain why a biased sample can distort the estimate.
options.virtualChange: Author the bias rule and comparison; the population chapter supports the assumptions, not this exact activity.

options.title: Estimate a plant population using quadrats
options.activity: Use random quadrats to estimate abundance/cover in an appropriate local area.
options.learningEvidence: Connect area samples with a justified population inference.
options.virtualChange: Redesign the virtual method from mobile-animal mark-recapture to quadrat sampling.

options.activity: Use the Gorongosa cards to build relationships and predict a disturbance effect.
options.learningEvidence: Explain the direction of energy flow using organism evidence.
options.virtualChange: Add a quantitative budget if replacing all of the current energy-calculation work.

options.title: Energy-token accounting through a web
options.activity: Move original counted tokens through transfers and record outputs and losses.

options.title: Model a trophic cascade
options.activity: Use the published activity to test the consequences of a predator change.
options.learningEvidence: Explain indirect effects across multiple trophic levels.
options.virtualChange: Redesign around abundance/interaction predictions rather than only an energy budget.

labs.decisionNote: There is a direct original printed-map extension and two strong published conservation options with different decision/evidence tasks.

options.title: Printed reserve-design map and budget
options.activity: Use the existing fictional map with original protection tokens and a fixed budget.
options.learningEvidence: Justify habitat/connectivity tradeoffs from a documented plan.
options.virtualChange: Create classroom turn/scoring/report rules; the current printable map alone is not a finished classroom protocol.

options.title: Interpret real fragmentation and corridor evidence
options.activity: Analyze the published scientific figure and compare fragmented/connected treatments.
options.learningEvidence: Separate empirical support from a reserve-planning prediction.
options.virtualChange: Add experimental-data interpretation to the virtual or use it to evaluate the current model’s limits.

options.virtualChange: Broaden the virtual from grid optimization to open-ended conservation planning if this becomes the core activity.

rejectedOrLimited.example: Simple sieve or muddy-water kidney filter
rejectedOrLimited.reason: Useful for a filtration analogy, but it does not account for selective reabsorption or secretion. Not recommended as a complete counterpart to the current nephron learning goals.

rejectedOrLimited.example: Human/frog diagrams used interchangeably with the current sea-urchin example
rejectedOrLimited.reason: Organism-specific movements and structures differ. A new context requires a coordinated redesign, not swapped illustrations.

rejectedOrLimited.example: A digital-only epidemic simulator described as a physical classroom activity
rejectedOrLimited.reason: A website resource is not itself an offline class model. Only an explicitly authored paper/network adaptation would satisfy that goal.

rejectedOrLimited.example: Uncontrolled culturing of unknown classroom/environmental microbes
rejectedOrLimited.reason: Not a proposed option. Prefer prepared evidence, images or a separately approved educational protocol.
